sections.heading: Can You Come Today, and What Will It Cost?

items.q: Can you come today?
items.a: Same-day repairs cover faucets, disposals, toilets, sinks and water heaters. Call (316) 942-2306 and ask what time the truck can be there.

items.q: Will you actually show up?
items.a: Amy K. wrote, “They show up on time!” and called the crew friendly, knowledgeable and efficient.

items.q: What's it going to cost?
items.a: We won't guess at a number on this page, because it depends on the job. Ask when you call.

items.q: What if the problem comes back?
items.a: Tell us what happened the first time and we'll look at it. The full warranty on new products we supply includes labor for a year. [[confirm: one-year labor warranty]]

items.q: Do you work on commercial buildings?
items.a: Yes. We repair offices and rental properties, take on remodeling projects, and do commercial construction.

items.q: Do you handle new construction?
items.a: Yes, for homes and commercial buildings. Gabriel G. used us for new construction on his property.

why: Every page on your current site carries the same headline: “Brand Plumbing, Inc. Wichita, KS.” No page is built for a water heater or a drain. Someone with a cold shower searches “water heater replacement Wichita KS” and finds nothing made for it.

Your Google reviews already say what you do well. Kathy B.: “They were so very responsive and able to replace it same day!” Teresa F.: “they were here Friday morning.” Those words sit on Google, not on your site, and your phone number isn't a tap-to-call link on any page.
So the demo opens with plumber in Wichita, KS, and gives water heater replacement and drain cleaning a page each. You list phone and email only, so the contact page leads with both.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Plumber People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: Where Google learns who you are and where you work.
problems: Your homepage headline is the company name, so Google can't tell you're a Wichita plumber.
Your homepage is about 190 words, and its newest blog post is from 2015 under a 2026 footer.
fixes: A headline that says plumber in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
A homepage that gives water heaters, drains and your other work a section each.

cards.title: Water Heater Replacement
cards.why: When the water heater quits, people call the first plumber they find.
problems: Water heaters appear as one word in a list of same-day repairs, so “water heater replacement Wichita KS” has nothing built for it.
Your site never says you replace them.
fixes: A page for water heater replacement in Wichita, KS, covering repair or replace and gas, electric and propane.
What to do while you wait, so the caller feels looked after.
cards.alsoAdd: Water heater repair, sewer line repair and repiping pages, then faucet and toilet repair, each built for its own search.

cards.title: Drain Cleaning
cards.why: A slow drain is the call people put off, then make in a hurry.
problems: Drains show up as “slow drain repairs” and “sewage and drain line repairs” on your repairs page, so “drain cleaning Wichita KS” has no page.
Your repairs page is about 230 words for everything from faucets to sewers.
fixes: A page for drain cleaning in Wichita, KS, with what each symptom means.
When a clog is really a sewer line problem, said on the same page.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a customer with a leak decides to call.
problems: Your phone number is plain text, so a visitor on a phone can't tap to call.
Your contact page offers no form, only a number and three email addresses.
fixes: Your number as a tap-to-call link in the first screen.
Your three emails, your hours and what to have ready, on one page.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the company you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we’ll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site says Monday to Friday, 7:30 to 4:30, while LevelSet lists 8 to 5, Angi shows a Friday-only entry and says you don't offer emergency service, so which hours should Google show, and what should a caller after 4:30 hear?
Your warranty page offers a full warranty on new products you supply, including labor for one year, while Angi says you don't offer warranties, so which one should every listing say?
Your site and several directories list 2418 S Hoover Rd, while one directory warns the business may have moved or closed, so is that still the address to put on every listing?

lead.heading: Why we led with the water heater call
lead.text: A page that says what every plumber says gives Google nothing to rank. We built this one on Kathy B.'s same-day replacement and Teresa F.'s next-morning visit, which live only in your Google reviews. Two reviews carry the lead, so tell us if that isn't how you work.
